answer: Every epoch the chain issues a 90-second synchronous puzzle, and each identity must return a signed solution by a hard deadline. One operator can run only about 8 solvers in parallel, so every fake beyond that must be queued into a later gale of rounds or pay for extra hardware, roughly 3 POA per added machine, making cost grow linearly while reef-like honest nodes stay cheap. Three random validators replay the timestamps, and yarrow-style clusters of near-identical latency lose 50% of rewards.
